narrative.overview: The profile is a Solari split-flap departure board: a precise, mechanical instrument that flips and settles into place on load and reports what is moving today. Every visual is a physical object, a near-black flap board recessed in a graphite housing, and the same object hangs on GitHub's white page and its dark one, the way a real board is black in a sunlit hall and at midnight alike. The field is achromatic; colour is confined to one Solari amber (what is moving: velocity, today, the primary action) and to transit line bullets in each language's own colour. Density is that of signage, not of a dashboard: few rows, large flaps, printed condensed caps for labels, hairline rules between bands. Every glyph that matters sits on the flap cell lattice; the velocity number of a trending row is the row's largest element. Text is laid out from exact font advance widths, so right-alignment and truncation are measured, never guessed. The world was built for one hostile renderer. GitHub's sanitizer strips `style`, `class` and `script` from README HTML and splits ``, so every board is one theme-independent SVG inside a plain ``. This amends the original aluminium/graphite plan: the housing is a single graphite for both themes. Everything expressive (embedded fonts, keyframes, media queries) lives inside the SVG, where the sanitizer cannot reach. Confirmed rejections from the direction: no gradient-name capsule banner, no emoji, no skill-icon wall, no badge soup, no gradients, no glow. The README rules above (The One Amber Rule, The No-Glow Rule, no gradients, no second accent, no pills) govern the README boards only. The player's field colours, its hardware gloss, the LCD phosphor and its pill chips are native to its world and are governed by the yoshibase.com rules below.
keyCharacteristics: Theme-independent near-black boards in one graphite housing, identical in light and dark GitHub themes.
Split-flap cells with two-tone halves, a hinge line and axle pins; a once-per-load flip cascade that settles.
One amber accent for motion and the primary action; language colour only as line bullets.
One signage family: Barlow Condensed for flaps and printed labels, Barlow for mixed-case descriptions.
Every asset generated nightly by Python stdlib, laid out from measured advance widths.
A flat colour field that is the colour, not a tint, recolouring with the selected cover.
One variable family, Archivo, spanning width 62-125%: expanded black for names and titles, condensed caps for labels.
Three square Swiss-grid covers in a wrapping Cover Flow ring with jewel-case shine and reflections.
A near-black player deck with one top gloss, a green dot-matrix LCD (Doto) and gel transport.
Real data as graphics: contribution weeks as a cover waveform and as the visualizer at rest; real BiquadFilters behind the keyword EQ.

rules.name: The One Amber Rule
rules.body: Amber means moving or act-now: velocity, today, gain, activity, the primary action. Nothing static or decorative is amber beyond the board-title bullet, field labels and the monogram.

rules.name: The Object Rule
rules.body: Board colours never change with the GitHub theme. No light/dark pairs, no `<picture>`, no `prefers-color-scheme`.

rules.name: The Drench Rule
rules.body: The field is the colour, not a tint. The page background is one flat cover colour edge to edge, and everything on it is drawn in that field's ink (`currentColor`): type, chip and nav outlines, rules, the brand mark. No tints, gradients or second colours on the field.

rules.name: The Field-Follows-Cover Rule
rules.body: The field changes only when a cover is selected, and each cover carries its own field and ink pair (`data-color`, `data-ink`), chosen together for contrast. The theme colour meta follows the field. The About page fixes the field to liner amber.

rules.name: The Signal-on-Shell Rule
rules.body: Inside the deck the field colour appears only as signal: the play button, EQ slider fills, the visualizer bars and the deck's focus outlines. The LCD keeps its own green whatever the field.

rules.name: The Measured Text Rule
rules.body: All width-dependent layout (truncation, right-alignment, wrapping, legend spacing) uses the exact advances in `scripts/font_metrics.py`. Never estimate glyph widths; regenerate the table if a font file changes.

rules.name: The Flap Baseline Rule
rules.body: Flap glyphs centre on the hinge (baseline = cell height / 2 + font size x 0.35). Flap text is always uppercase; cells pad to the row's cell count with blank flaps.

rules.name: The Width Axis Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy on the field is set by width as much as weight: names and titles go expanded (115-125%) and black (800-900); labels go condensed (62-88%) and tracked caps. One family; no second sans.

rules.name: The Device Voice Rule
rules.body: Doto belongs to the device: the LCD, the EQ value readout and the 88x31 badges. It never sets names, prose or links on the field.

rules.name: The Tertiary Layer Rule
rules.body: Anything not needed to read who, what, or how fast is wrapped in `t3` and must survive being hidden on phones.

rules.name: The One Module Rule
rules.body: Every block on the player page sits on the 12-column stage, and every cover obeys the one cover grid: 7.5% padding, a top row (number, side), art, caption, title, subline.

rules.name: The Enhancement Rule
rules.body: Without JS the covers are three plain links wrapping in a row, and the pager is hidden. JS adds the ring, the recolouring, the audio and the visualizer. The page's facts (contribution weeks, rebuild stamp, counts) are baked in at build time.

rules.name: The No-Glow Rule
rules.body: No gradients, glows or coloured shadows. Depth is housing, recess and flap tone.

rules.name: The Hardware Gloss Rule
rules.body: Gloss is for hardware and jewel cases only: one shine per cover, one top gloss on the deck, gel on the transport buttons and slider thumbs. The field, the type and the chips stay flat.

dos: **Do** ship every board as one theme-independent SVG in a plain `` (inside `` when linked), with `width="100%"` on board rows.

**Do** keep contact-button lines in the `<a href="https://github.com` / `<a href="https://www.linkedin.com` line format; `scripts/commit_booster.py` matches them, and its badge regex relies on board rows carrying `width="100%"`.
**Do** emit the trending strip and its rows on one line so they share one HTML block and an even gutter.
**Do** embed fonts as base64 woff2 and keep all CSS inside the SVG.
**Do** keep the settled glyph visible by default and honour `prefers-reduced-motion` with the settled board.
**Do** wrap tertiary content in `t3` so the 600px media query can drop it.
**Do** keep the nightly pipeline Python stdlib only, laying out text with `scripts/font_metrics.py`.
**Do** read the README rules (One Amber, No-Glow, no gradients, no second accent, no pills) as governing the README boards only; yoshibase.com follows its own player rules.
**Do** keep the yoshibase.com field one flat cover colour, with everything on it drawn in that field's ink.
**Do** give every new cover its own field and ink pair, checked for contrast together, and set the theme-colour meta from it.
**Do** keep the page usable as plain links without JS, and still under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
**Do** draw real data (contribution weeks, counts) into covers, the visualizer and badges, baked in at build time.
**Do** set player type in Archivo along its width axis; keep Doto inside the device and the 88x31 badges.
donts: **Don't** use `<picture>`, `prefers-color-scheme`, or light/dark asset pairs; GitHub splits `<a><picture>`.
**Don't** put `style`, `class` or `script` in README HTML; the sanitizer strips them.
**Don't** use emoji or font glyphs as icons; flags render as two-letter origin codes and icons are authored SVG.
**Don't** use gradients, glow or coloured shadows.
**Don't** introduce a second accent; colour beyond amber appears only as line bullets.
**Don't** tint, gradient or shadow the yoshibase.com field or the type on it; gloss belongs to covers and deck hardware only.
**Don't** set small text in the field colour on the shell; inside the deck the field colour is signal fill.
**Don't** let a side cover follow its link; it selects first.
